newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westfield Trust plans to match H1 payment.
newsitem.headline: Westfield Trust plans to match H1 payment.

text.p: Shopping centre owner Westfield Trust said its distribution in the second half of calendar 1997 was expected to at least match the 9.97 cents per unit paid in the first half, barring unforeeen circumstances.
The company said in a note accompanying its first half result that the distribution represented a rise of two percent on the year-ago level and amounted to A$118.7 million.

Westfield Trust's net profit rose to A$122 million from A$108.3 million a year earlier, with the latest period including an abnormal profit of A$3.3 million on the sale of a half share in the West Lakes centre in Adelaide.
The company said retail sales in its portfolio of stores was A$5.9 billion in the six months ended June 30, a rise of 13.5 percent on the year-ago level and 2.3 percent higher on a comparable basis.
It said continuing demand by retailers for space in Westfield centres saw the vacancy level remain at less than one percent of retail space.
